svg.text: Read-only w.r.t. the base pipeline above (F) -- lets a human correct what it missed, then retrains the SAME model (E) reuses for the next round

text.tspan: Figure 1. UNIFIED single-model crack-detection pipeline for SEM/TXM micrographs of annealed stainless steel, plus its manual-correction and retraining loop.
Raw 16-bit micrographs are contrast-stretched and auto-cropped (A), background-flattened (B), and segmented into candidate dark regions (C). A Frangi
vesselness filter and connected-component analysis extract an 11-feature vector per candidate (D) -- 9 real (size, shape, brightness, vesselness) plus 2
neutral placeholders for the two crack-context features (distance to / boundary contact with a confirmed crack) that cannot yet be computed before any
candidate has been confirmed. ONE shared 11-feature logistic-regression classifier -- the SAME .joblib file reused again in stage (H) -- separates these
into cracks and artifacts; a minimum-spanning-tree bridges fragments of the same physical crack (E), producing a Pass-1 mask, overlay, and measurements (F).
Read-only against that result, a human can then directly add, correct, or erase regions in a browser paint app (red=crack/cyan=artifact/magenta=erase, two
touching red regions always merge into one crack) or work through review sheets of harder candidates the base mask's brightness threshold missed -- notches
along a crack's own boundary, corridors between bridged fragments, or the wider gradient-fade interior a flattening filter can suppress (G). Those
candidates get their REAL crack-context features computed relative to the now-real Pass-1 crack mask, and are scored by the SAME shared model from (E) plus
an extra calibrated distance/brightness rule for the hardest candidate type, leave-one-out validated against every known negative; accepted regions are
folded into the crack mask, and the freshly labeled corrections (both original-candidate and interior-candidate) retrain that one shared model for the next
round (H). Using one model instead of two collapses a training-data split that no longer reflected a real architectural difference between candidate types
-- see MODEL_VALIDATION_BENCHMARK.md for the cross-validated evidence this performs comparably to the previous two-model system. Worked example shown:
